missing_evidence: No source here directly addresses a digital tablet or whether Torah text displayed electronically gives the device the status of a Sefer Torah or printed sefer.
No source here gives a specific ruling for kissing an electronic Torah tablet as a custom.

paragraphs.text: The sources that speak about kissing describe a custom tied to the Sefer Torah when it is carried or shown to the congregation, and the reason given is education and honor for the Torah scroll, not a rule about any object containing Torah text. Therefore, these sources support respect while using the tablet, but not a claim that kissing it is an established Sefer-Torah practice.
But other authorities in the same material already limit or criticize how that is done, showing that even with a real Sefer Torah the practice is a custom of honor, not an absolute requirement.

The sources also show that words of Torah themselves are not susceptible to impurity, and even people in states of ritual impurity may hold and read a Sefer Torah. That tells us the holiness in these sources is not a physical impurity-status that can simply be transferred from Torah content to every object that displays it.

What is clearly supported is general kavod haTorah: one should sit before Torah with seriousness, honor it as much as possible, and honor Torah study. So if someone uses the tablet for learning, treating it respectfully is appropriate.
There is also a useful distinction in the sources between the sacred text and the physical object holding it.
If one wants to show respect while learning from it, that is supported in a general way by kavod haTorah; but equating it with a Sefer Torah is not supported here.

question_html:
Kiss a Torah Tablet?

There are tablets sold, eg by artscroll, preloaded with Torah and have blocked all access to anything else except things that aid learning like alarms etc.

Is it appropriate, or inappropriate to kiss this tablet when using it like a sefer? Is it even permitted?

research_plan.context: This is a halacha/kavod haTorah question about whether a digital tablet preloaded with Torah text should be treated like a sefer, especially regarding the custom of kissing a sacred text. A key premise to test is whether Torah content on an electronic device creates any inherent kedushah comparable to a Sefer Torah or printed sefarim, or whether the relevant issue is only proper respect while using it for learning.
subquestions: Does Torah text displayed electronically have any halakhic kedushah, or only functional significance for study?
What is the source and scope of the custom to kiss a Sefer Torah or sefer, and does it extend to non-book media?
If the device is used only for Torah learning, is kissing it merely a permissible expression of respect, or is it discouraged because it is not a sacred object?
Are there sources distinguishing between Sefer Torah, printed chumash/sefer, and nonphysical or electronic Torah content?

sources.relevance_reason: Primary halachic source for the custom of honoring/kissing the Sefer Torah; includes the Rema's note that children come to kiss it as chinuch, showing the practice is tied to a real Sefer Torah service context rather than generic Torah content.
sources.text:
he: שהצבו' לא יצאו מב"ה עד שיצניעו ס"ת. ובו סעיף אחד: אין הצבור רשאים לצאת מב"ה עד שיצניעו ס"ת [מיהו אם אינם יוצאים רק יחיד לית לן בה] (ב"י בשם הר"י בחידושי מגילה) ואם מצניעים הס"ת בבית אחר אם אין לב"ה אלא פתח א' צריכין להתעכב עד שיצא הס"ת וילכו אחריו למקום שמצניעין אותו שם ואם יש לב"ה שני פתחי' יכולים לצאת בפתח אחד קודם שיצא הס"ת בפתח האח' ובלבד שילכו אחר הס"ת וילוהו למקום שמצניעין אותו שם: הגה ובמקומות שמצניעין אותו בהיכל שהוא הארון בב"ה מצוה לכל מי שעוברת לפניו ללותה עד לפני הארון שמכניסין אותו שם [ד"ע ומהרי"ל] וכן הגולל ילך אחר הס"ת עד לפני הארון ועומד שם עד שיחזירו הס"ת למקומה [הג"מ פי"ב מה"ת וכן נוהגין במגביה הס"ת כי הוא עיקר הגולל וכמו שנתבאר סי' קמ"ז ס"ד ויש שכתבו שבאים התינוקות לנשק התורה כדי לחנכם ולזרזם במצות וכן נוהגין [אור זרוע]:

en: The Congregation May Not Leave The Synagogue Until they Conceal the Torah Scroll. Containing 1 S'if: The congregation does not have permission to leave the synagogue until after they conceal the Torah scroll. (However, if they are all not leaving, but it's just an individual that is, then that is not an issue) (Beit Yosef in the name of the R'i in Chidushei Megillah). And if they conceal the Torah in another house: if the synagogue has only one entrance, then they must delay until the Torah scroll has left and then they should go after it to the place in which they conceal it. If the synagogue has 2 entrances, they may leave using one entrance before the Torah scroll leaves using the other entrance, as long as they will go after the sefer Torah and escort it to the place where they conceal it. Gloss: And in places where they conceal it in the "heikhal", which is the cabinet [i.e. Ark] within the synagogue, it is a obligation for anyone in front of whom it [i.e. the Torah] passes to escort it up until [it is] in front of the Ark into which they are inserting it (His own opinion, and Mahari"l). And so too, the one who rolls the sefer Torah should go after the Torah until in front of the Ark and stand there until they return the Torah to its place. (Hagahot Maimoni - chapter 12 of Hilkhot Torah). And similarly, we practice that the one who lifts the sefer Torah [follows as well] since this is [considered] the main "roller" as we explained in Siman 147: S'if 4. And there are those who have written that the children come to kiss the Torah in order to educate them and train them to be zealous in [doing] mitzvot, and that is how we practice. (Ohr Zaruah)

he: המפטיר בנביא הוא פורס על שמע באיזה שמע אמרו בשמע של ספר תורה היכי פתח אשרי יושבי ביתך ואח"כ עומד המפטיר ואומר (תהלים פו) אין כמוך באלהים ה' ואין כמעשיך (שמות ט״ו:י״א) מי כמוך באלים ה׳ מי כמוך נאדר בקדש נורא תהלות עושה פלא (תהילים קמ״ה:י״ג-י״ד) מלכותך מלכות כל עולמים וממשלתך בכל דור ודור. ה׳ מלך ה׳ מלך (שמות ט״ו:י״ח) ה' ימלוך לעולם ועד (ישעיהו מ״ב:כ״א) ה׳ חפץ למען צדקו יגדיל תורה ויאדיר (תהילים כ״ט:י״א) ה׳ עוז לעמו יתן ה' יברך את עמו בשלום (נחמיה ט׳:ו׳) אתה הוא [ה'] לבדך אתה עשית את השמים שמי השמים וכל צבאם הארץ וכל אשר עליה הימים וכל אשר בהם ואתה מחיה את כולם וצבא השמים לך משתחוים:

en: The mafṭir recites also the parts of the Shema‘ . 18 This is explained below. The recitation of the Shema‘ is deemed to be a great honour which compensates for the lesser dignity conferred by the reading of the hafṭarah . Of what Shema‘ has this been said? 19 The Shema‘ is recited several times during the service. Of the one [recited when] the scroll of the Torah [is taken from the ark]. 20 Cf. the next Rule. How does one begin? 21 The collection of Biblical verses recited when the Torah scroll is taken from the ark. Happy are they that dwell in Thy house . 22 Ps. 84, 5. Then the mafṭir stands and recites, There is none like unto Thee among the gods, O Lord; and there are no works like Thine . 23 ibid. LXXXVI, 8. Who is like unto Thee, O Lord, among the mighty? Who is like unto Thee, glorious in holiness, fearful in praises, doing wonders? 24 Ex. 15, 11. Thy kingdom is a kingdom for all ages, and Thy dominion endureth throughout all generations . 25 Ps. 145, 13. The Lord is King, the Lord hath reigned, the Lord shall reign for ever and ever . 26 Compounded from Ps. 10, 16, XCIII, 1 (E.V. reigneth ) and Ex. 15, 18. The Lord was pleased, for His righteousness’ sake, to make the teaching great and glorious . 27 Isa. 42, 21. The Lord will give strength unto His people; the Lord will bless His people with peace . 28 Ps. 29, 11. Thou art the Lord, even Thou alone; Thou hast made heaven, the heaven of heavens, with all their host, the earth and all things that are therein, the seas and all that is in them and Thou preservest them all; and the host of heaven worshippeth Thee . 29 Neh. 9, 6.

he: כְּבוֹד תּוֹרָה קָאָמְרַתְּ. כְּבוֹד תּוֹרָה דְּיָחִיד — חָמוּר, תַּלְמוּד תּוֹרָה דְּיָחִיד — קַל.

en: The Gemara rejects this argument: You speak of the honor that must be shown to the Torah, and indeed, the honor that must be shown to the Torah in the case of an individual Torah scholar is important; but the Torah study of an individual in itself is light and is less significant than the Temple service.
